newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Enel H1 pre-tax profit climbs.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Enel H1 pre-tax profit climbs.

text.p: Italian electricity giant Enel, slated for privatisation in 1997, said its pre-tax profit rose to 2.99 trillion lire in the first half of the year against 2.54 trillion lire in the same period last year.
The company said in a statement that it expected its full year result would be roughly in line with its 1995 performance.
The government cut electricity tariffs at the start of July, but Enel said in its statement that it had covered the subsequent loss of revenue thanks to new, unspecified measures.
Enel, one of the largest electricity firms in Europe, said its operating result in the first six months of the year totalled 4.54 trillion lire against a previous 4.45 trillion.
It added that it had cut its debt level by 2.52 trillion lire between January and June. At the end of December, Enel's debt totalled 35.1 trillion lire.
The statement said it expected a further fall in debt by the end of the year but not of the same size as the fall seen in the first six months.

The reduction in debt was partly brought about by an increase in the compnay's ability to self-finance itself, with self-financing climbing to 6.2 trillion lire versus 5.86 trillion lire at the end of June 1995.
Electricity sales rose by 1.6 percent in the first half while personnel costs fell by 1.4 percent over the same period.
